- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 68.5), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +2–3% below peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.20) and price is trending up, model overestimates — apply downward bias of 1–3% to 3-day horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 68.0, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.30), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often underestimates downside risk — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for 1–3 days ahead.
